title: Fix it: send an xml document inside a json envelope
basics: `write(value, "application/xml")` turns a value into XML text, a String, which can then be placed inside a JSON field like any other String. A third argument passes writer properties, such as `{ indent: false, writeDeclaration: false }`, which control how the text is laid out.
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

A logistics partner accepts orders as JSON, but the order itself must be an XML document in a String field:

```
{ "ref": "O-1", "xml": "<order><id>O-1</id><line>A</line></order>" }
```

The payload is `{ id, lines }`, where `lines` is an array of SKUs. Build the envelope with `ref` set to the id, and `xml` holding an `order` element with one `id` and one `line` element per SKU, written on one line with no XML declaration.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
starter:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  ref: payload.id,
  xml: write({ order: { id: payload.id, line: payload.lines } }, "application/xml", { indent: false, writeDeclaration: false })
}
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
writes the lines unconditionally, and an empty Array still produces one empty line element
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  ref: payload.id,
  xml: write({ order: { id: payload.id, (line: payload.lines) if (!isEmpty(payload.lines)) } }, "application/xml", { indent: false, writeDeclaration: false })
}

mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  ref: payload.id,
  xml: write({ order: { id: payload.id, line: payload.lines } }, "application/xml", { indent: false, writeDeclaration: false })
}

explanation.approach: Embedding one format in another means serialising the inner document to a String first, which is what `write` does. The value written has to be a valid XML shape, with a single root, and the writer properties go in the third argument. The hidden trap is the empty order: an empty Array under `line` does not vanish, it becomes one empty `<line/>`, so the field has to be left out when there are no lines.

snippets.label: write returns text
snippets.note: In the JSON output, it is an ordinary String field.

snippets.label: The default layout
snippets.note: A declaration and line breaks, unless you turn them off.

snippets.label: An empty Array is not nothing
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
write({ order: { line: [] } }, "application/xml", { indent: false, writeDeclaration: false })
snippets.note: One empty element, which the partner reads as a line with no SKU.

snippets.label: Two roots
snippets.note: An XML document needs exactly one root element.

snippets.label: An Array becomes repeated elements
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0

write({ order: { line: ["A", "B"] } }, "application/xml", { indent: false, writeDeclaration: false })
